newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador unions threaten to go back on warpath.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador unions threaten to go back on warpath.

text.p: Ecuador's trade unions threatened to resume their battle plan May 1 if new President Fabian Alarcon keeps up his predecessor's policies, local media reported on Sunday.

The daily El Comercio said after a national assembly held on Saturday the unions warned they were analyzing the possibility of re-launching the protests which led to the ouster of former President Abdala Bucaram.
Bucaram was voted out of Congress on Feb. 6 on grounds of "mental incompetence" after just six months in office.
His departure capped a long string of street protests against economic austerity measures and was decided at the end of a 48-hour general strike.

Local media said the trade unions were pressing Alarcon to heed a document he signed before swearing in as president, in which he agreed to oppose neoliberal policies and the privatization of the country's key energy resources.
